machines.name: OTTO-CHARGE ARM
summary: A 6-axis robot arm at each fast charger.
It finds the charge port, pushes the DC connector in and locks it.
It lets go when the charge ends. The car cannot move until the arm is home.
owner: A robot arm plugs your car in and unplugs it. No person handles the cable.
The arm measures the force on every move. A small error cannot jam the connector.
Your car cannot move until the arm is home.

facts.label: Connector
facts.value: DC combo class (CCS), liquid-cooled

facts.label: Charge cable
facts.value: 500 A DC, liquid-cooled

facts.label: Time to connect
facts.value: 18.5 s of arm motion

facts.label: Time to release
facts.value: 11.5 s of arm motion

facts.label: Finds the port
facts.value: Stereo cameras and a time-of-flight sensor find the inlet. A light ring helps at night.

facts.label: Force control
facts.value: A 6-axis force and torque sensor reads the insertion force. A compliance unit lets the connector float up to 6 mm and 3 degrees. A small error cannot jam it.

facts.label: Latch
facts.value: A solenoid latch locks the connector in the inlet for the charge.

facts.label: Cable
facts.value: The charge cable comes up out of the cabinet roof into a take-up wheel. A spring keeps the cable off the car.

facts.label: Status lights
facts.value: Light rings on the arm show its state: teal ready, amber moving, green charging, red fault.

safety: A safety laser scanner on the riser watches the stall at knee height. A person in its field stops the arm.
An emergency stop on the riser cuts motor power (safe torque off).
OTTO-Q does not move a car while an arm is connected to it.
When a charger has a fault, the arm lets the car go at once. OTTO-Q sends the car to another charger.

machines.name: OTTO-CLEAN ARM
summary: An overhead arm over each fast charger. It vacuums the cabin while the car charges.
It swings in a plane 1.8 m above the roof. Only the wand goes into the car, and only through a door.
The doors open. The arm cleans one side, then the other side. Then the doors close.
owner: An overhead arm vacuums the cabin of your car while it charges.
Only the wand goes into the car, and only through an open door.
Every part of the arm keeps 0.10 m off the bodywork and the open doors.
Your car stays at its charger until the arm is home.

facts.label: Nozzle head
facts.value: Cleans the floor, the benches and the seat backs with vacuum, an air knife and a brush lip.

facts.label: Time for a clean
facts.value: About 6 min: 2.5 min on each side, and the moves between. The twin sets the time.

facts.label: Reach
facts.value: The wand reaches 1.37 m into the cabin.

facts.label: Mast
facts.value: Lowers the wrist from 2.18 m to 0.58 m above grade, beside the car, never over it.

facts.label: Clearance
facts.value: 0.10 m off the car and the open doors, at every point of the cycle.

facts.label: Vacuum supply
facts.value: A central vacuum producer on each canopy (about 3 kW per working arm, 30 kPa class) serves its arms.

facts.label: Crew
facts.value: The arm needs no technician.

facts.label: Status lights
facts.value: Lights on the base, the mast and the nozzle show the arm state.

safety: The arm swings above the roof. Nothing stands where a car drives.
The car stays on its stall until the arm is home.
A brake holds the mast when power is off.
A charger fault lets the car go at once. The arm at the next charger does the clean.

machines.name: OTTO-WASH
summary: A rollover machine in each wash bay. It moves over the parked car 6 times.
The passes are: pre-soak, 2 brush passes, rinse, 2 dry passes.
On a detail seat, 2 vacuum wands clean the cabin first.
owner: A machine washes your car in the wash bay. It moves over the parked car 6 times.
The passes are pre-soak, 2 brush passes, rinse and 2 dry passes.
On a detail visit, 2 vacuum wands clean the cabin first, through the open doors.

steps.label: The car stops under the light

facts.label: Passes
facts.value: 6 passes in about 3.5 min: pre-soak, 2 brush passes, rinse, 2 dry passes.

facts.label: Cabin vacuum
facts.value: On a detail seat, about 10 min before the wash. The twin sets the time.

facts.label: Top brush
facts.value: Washes the bonnet, the roof and the roof pod. It follows the car top.

facts.label: Side brushes
facts.value: Wash the flanks, the doors and the wheels.

facts.label: Spray arch
facts.value: Sprays the pre-soak foam, then the clear-water rinse. 9 flat-fan nozzles each side and 5 across the top.

facts.label: Air knives
facts.value: Blow the water off in the last 2 passes. Blowers: top 4 kW, sides 2 x 3 kW (class).

facts.label: Travel speed
facts.value: about 10 m/min

facts.label: Stop light
facts.value: A stop light faces the arriving car: red while the program runs, green when the car may go.

facts.label: Supply
facts.value: A drag chain brings power, water, chemicals and air. It lies in a covered trench in the floor, inboard of the west rail.

facts.label: Clear height
facts.value: 3.30 m under the beam

safety: Retracted, everything clears a car by more than 0.48 m.
The machine never moves over the car with a tool still on it.
A stop at each rail end holds a wheel if the machine runs past its travel.
The car leaves only when the light is green.
